title: UNIT 5: VECTORS
notes:
✓ Vector → a quantity having both magnitude and direction.

✓ Scalar → a quantity described only by magnitude.

Vector → represented by an arrow, with length showing magnitude and arrowhead showing direction.

Main topics → representation of vectors, vector operations, scalar multiplication, unit vectors, magnitude and direction, parallel/equal vectors, dot product, and vectors in three-dimensional space.

title: 5.1 REPRESENTATION OF VECTORS
notes:
✓ A vector can be represented geometrically by a directed line segment.

◆ Initial point → starting point of a vector.
◆ Terminal point → ending point.

If a vector starts at P(x₁,y₁) and ends at Q(x₂,y₂):

v = PQ = (x₂ − x₁, y₂ − y₁)

Example:
P(1,2), Q(6,7)

v = (6−1, 7−2)
  = (5,5).

If the initial point is the origin:
v = (x,y).

title: 5.2 VECTOR ADDITION AND SUBTRACTION
notes:
✓ Vector addition → join vectors head-to-tail; the resultant joins the first tail to the final head.

If u = (u₁,u₂) and v = (v₁,v₂):

u + v = (u₁ + v₁, u₂ + v₂)

Example:
u = (2,5), v = (7,3)

u + v = (9,8).

◆ Subtraction:
u − v = u + (−v)

Therefore:
u − v = (u₁−v₁, u₂−v₂).

title: 5.2.3 SCALAR MULTIPLICATION
notes:
✓ Scalar multiplication → multiplying a vector by a real number k.

If v = (x,y):
kv = (kx,ky).

Example:
v = (−1,3)

7v = (−7,21).

◆ k > 0 → direction remains the same.
◆ k < 0 → direction is reversed.
◆ |k| → changes the magnitude by a factor of |k|.
◆ k = 0 → zero vector.

Magnitude:
|kv| = |k||v|.

title: 5.2.4 UNIT VECTORS
notes:
✓ Unit vector → a vector whose magnitude is 1.

Standard unit vectors:
i = (1,0)
j = (0,1)

Therefore:
(x,y) = xi + yj.

Example:
v = (2,3)

v = 2i + 3j.

A vector can be written in component form using i and j.

Unit vector in the direction of v:
v̂ = v/|v|,  v ≠ 0.

title: MAGNITUDE, DIRECTION AND EQUALITY
notes:
For v = (x,y):

✓ Magnitude/norm:
|v| = √(x² + y²)

Example:
v = (3,4)

|v| = √(3²+4²) = 5.

◆ Two vectors are equal if they have the same magnitude and direction.

◆ The negative vector −v has the same magnitude as v but opposite direction.

◆ Zero vector:
0 = (0,0).

Direction can be described by the inclination of the vector or by the slope when appropriate.

title: PARALLEL VECTORS
notes:
✓ Two non-zero vectors u and v are parallel if one is a non-zero scalar multiple of the other.

Condition:
u = kv,  k ≠ 0.

Example:
u = (2,4)
v = (1,2)

Since:
u = 2v

→ u and v are parallel and point in the same direction.

If k < 0 → vectors are parallel but point in opposite directions.

Example:
u = (−2,−4) = −2(1,2).

title: 5.3 VECTOR PRODUCT: SCALAR (DOT) PRODUCT
notes:
✓ The scalar or dot product of two vectors produces a scalar.

If u and v make an angle θ:

u · v = |u||v|cosθ

Example:
|u| = 8, |v| = 7, θ = 30°

u · v = 8(7)cos30°
      = 28√3.

→ Dot product is useful for finding angles and testing perpendicularity.

title: DOT PRODUCT IN COMPONENT FORM
notes:
If:
u = u₁i + u₂j
v = v₁i + v₂j

Then:
u · v = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂.

Example:
u = 5i + 3j
v = i + 2j

u · v = (5)(1) + (3)(2)
      = 11.

Angle between non-zero vectors:

cosθ = (u · v)/(|u||v|).

✓ If u · v = 0 → u and v are perpendicular (orthogonal).

title: IMPORTANT DOT PRODUCT PROPERTIES
notes:
◆ Commutative:
u · v = v · u

◆ Distributive:
u · (v + w) = u · v + u · w

◆ Scalar multiplication:
(ku) · v = k(u · v)

◆ A vector dotted with itself:
u · u = |u|².

◆ Perpendicular vectors:
u · v = 0.

◆ Angle formula:
cosθ = (u · v)/(|u||v|).

→ Same direction → dot product is positive.
→ Opposite direction → dot product is negative.
→ Perpendicular → dot product is zero.

title: 5.3.2 VECTORS IN THREE-DIMENSIONAL SPACE
notes:
✓ Three-dimensional space uses three mutually perpendicular axes:

◆ x-axis
◆ y-axis
◆ z-axis

A point is represented by:
P(x,y,z).

A vector in space can be written:
v = (x,y,z)

or:
v = xi + yj + zk.

Magnitude:
|v| = √(x² + y² + z²).

Example:
v = (2,3,6)

|v| = √(4+9+36)
   = 7.

title: UNIT 5 KEY FORMULAS & QUICK REVISION
notes:
◆ Vector from P(x₁,y₁) to Q(x₂,y₂):
PQ = (x₂−x₁, y₂−y₁).

◆ Addition:
u+v = (u₁+v₁, u₂+v₂).

◆ Subtraction:
u−v = (u₁−v₁, u₂−v₂).

◆ Scalar multiplication:
ku = (ku₁,ku₂).

◆ Magnitude:
|u| = √(u₁²+u₂²).

◆ Unit vector:
û = u/|u|.

◆ Parallel vectors:
u = kv, k ≠ 0.

◆ Dot product:
u·v = |u||v|cosθ.

◆ Component dot product:
u·v = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂.

◆ Angle:
cosθ = (u·v)/(|u||v|).

◆ Perpendicular:
u·v = 0.

◆ 3D magnitude:
|u| = √(u₁²+u₂²+u₃²).

✓ Core idea → vectors describe quantities with magnitude and direction and can be added, scaled, compared and multiplied using the dot product.
